title: Maximum acceleration calculation
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the maximum acceleration as 4 m/s², using the worker's weight as the maximum tension and applying Newton's second law to the object.

title: Velocity after 2 seconds
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the object's velocity (8 m/s) at the moment the rope breaks using kinematics with the previously found acceleration.

title: Height during acceleration phase
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the distance (8 m) the object travels upward during the 2-second period of constant acceleration.

title: Height after rope breaks
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the additional height (3.2 m) the object rises after the rope breaks, treating it as free fall under gravity.

title: Total maximum height
description: Essential: The student must correctly sum the two height contributions to obtain the final answer of 11.2 m.

title: Maximum tension identification
description: Important: The student must recognize that the maximum force the worker can exert equals their weight (Mg), which becomes the rope tension.

title: Newton's second law application
description: Optional: The student should clearly write the force balance equation (T - mg = ma) for the object, showing the direction of forces.

title: Sign error in kinematics
description: Pitfall: Deduct points if the student uses incorrect signs for acceleration or velocity in the kinematic equations after the rope breaks.

title: Confusion about maximum force
description: Pitfall: Deduct points if the student incorrectly assumes the maximum pulling force is (M+m)g or another incorrect value.
